facts.claim: Agreeableness is linked to a correlation coefficient of -0.12* to -0.353*** with higher levels of job burnout.
facts.quote: lower agreeableness (r from - 0. 12* to - 0. 353***; β from - 0. 08*** to - 0. 523*)

facts.claim: Agreeableness is linked to a correlation coefficient of 0.855 with marital satisfaction.
Agreeableness is linked to improved orthodontic outcomes and more favorable treatment attitudes.
facts.quote: positive traits, including extraversion, agreeableness, and conscientiousness, were correlated with improved orthodontic outcomes and more favorable treatment attitudes.

facts.claim: Agreeableness is linked to predicting positive affect as well as Extraversion.
facts.quote: Positive affect was predicted equally well by Extraversion and Agreeableness.

facts.claim: The Big Five traits were moderately associated with overall health (multiple R = . 35).
facts.quote: When entered simultaneously, the Big Five traits were moderately associated with overall health (multiple R = . 35).

research.angle: While agreeableness is linked to higher marital satisfaction and positive affect, lower agreeableness is linked to higher job burnout.
research.verdict: The evidence does not support the idea that high agreeableness leads to lower life satisfaction; instead, it is linked to higher marital satisfaction and positive affect.
research.caveat: The sources provide mixed results on how agreeableness impacts different types of well-being, such as marital satisfaction versus job burnout.
